contexts.text: As wine = faith in the Lord, in the Jewish Church, faith was represented in the sacrifices by a drink-offering of wine. Illustrated.
To pour a drink-offering upon the pillar () = the Divine good of faith.
They used to pour libations on the pillars.

(Jacob) poured a drink-offering upon it () = the Divine good of truth. A drink-offering = the Divine good of truth... The good of faith is what is signified by a drink-offering; and the good of love by oil.... This, therefore, namely, spiritual good or the good of faith, or the good of truth, is what is signified by a drink-offering. AC 4581:4, Illustrated.
The meat-offering and the drink-offering = the same as the bread and wine in the Holy Supper.
The meat-offering and the drink-offering were added to the burnt-offerings and sacrifices. Illustrated.

When they receded from the genuine representative of the worship of the Lord, and turned themselves to other gods, and poured drink-offerings to them, then drink-offerings = those things which are opposite to charity and faith, namely, the evils of the love of the world and the falsities. Illustrated.
To pour to them a drink-offering () = the worship of them. AC 10137:7.
To pour drink-offerings () = to worship. AC 4581:9.
Drink-offerings of blood are also mentioned in ... and by them are signified profanations of truth.
The wine of the drink-offering = the truth of faith thence.
The good of faith is the winepress, the must, and the drink-offering of wine ().
A drink-offering of the fourth part of a hin of wine () = spiritual truth as much as for conjunction.

Hence, when the meat-offering was offered, which was bread, a drink-offering was also offered, which was wine... Hence it is that by a drink-offering of wine is here meant the truth corresponding to the good which is signified by the meat-offering.
That the drink-offering, which was wine, = the good of faith. Illustrated.

A drink-offering ye shall not pour upon it () = that there was not there a representative of regeneration by the truths and goods of spiritual love. A drink-offering = a representative of regeneration by the truths and goods of faith and charity, which are the truths and goods of spiritual love.
Under Altar, see this reference.

The meat-offering and the drink-offering in the sacrifices had a like signification (to the bread and wine in the Holy Supper). Illustrated. The meat-offering was of fine flour of wheat; hence it was in place of the bread; and the drink-offering was of wine.
To sip her beauty. CL 330:3.
After they have sipped the sweetness of the innocence in their little children...
After the first enjoyment they reject them... Set on the left those they have enjoyed, and on the right those they have not enjoyed...
The meat-offering, which was bread, = good; and the drink-offering, which was wine, = truth, both from the Lord; for it is said from our God ().

The meat-offering was of bread, and the drink-offering was of wine, by which is signified the worship of the Lord from the good of love and from the truths thence derived; for all the worship of the Lord is from these.
In the opposite sense, by the meat-offering and the drink-offering is signified worship from the evils which are of the love of evil, and from the falsities of faith.
To pour out drink-offerings to other gods () = to worship from falsities.
The meat-offering () = the good of the Church; and the drink-offering, its truth.
